In April 2022, Governor Kathy Hochul announced an investment of $350 million for workforce development, including the creation of the Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) within ESD. OSWD is charged with better aligning workforce development efforts with the needs and priorities of today's employers. Through OSWD, ESD is helping to create new economic opportunities for unemployed, underemployed, and underrepresented workers, while simultaneously meeting the labor needs of the state's highest-growth sectors.

One of those sectors is Artificial Intelligence (AI), which is advancing rapidly across the globe, revolutionizing industries such as healthcare, finance, transportation, and manufacturing. Countries are investing heavily in AI research, automation, and machine learning to drive innovation and economic growth. New York State has emerged as a key hub for AI development, with institutions like Cornell Tech leading cutting-edge research. Companies in New York are leveraging AI for data analytics, automation, and decision-making, while state-backed initiatives, like Empire AI, support AI-driven advancements in medicine, infrastructure, and cybersecurity. These advancements promise increased efficiency, economic expansion, and groundbreaking solutions to complex societal problems.

However, the rapid advancement of AI also raises concerns about widening economic inequality, particularly for low-income individuals who may lack the skills or access needed to benefit from the AI-driven economy. Many well-paying AI-related jobs require specialized education and technical training, which are often out of reach for lower-income individuals. Without policies focused on AI education with equitable access to new opportunities, there is a risk that technological progress will disproportionately benefit those already in privileged positions, leaving underrepresented communities behind. By implementing AI Prep, New York will create opportunities in this critical sector while simultaneously reinforcing New York's position as a hub for innovation and economic opportunity.

item: solution.assumptions[1] (assumption): MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 is assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT's public Engineering Policy Guide and to be stable for the project term; we will encode it as a versioned ruleset and re-verify it at each review gate rather than assume it is supplied with the RFP.
evidence:
[S9.1]
[SECTION (1): GENERAL DESCRIPTION AND BACKGROUND > (B) Background, page 5]
**(B) Background:** The purpose of a property description is to accurately define certain land areas, or rights to be acquired, conveyed or leased. The description must recite specific rights being acquired, conveyed, or leased, if such rights are less than fee simple title, and be accurately described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls.

There are numerous methods in which land or rights can be described for the purpose of leasing, conveying or acquiring. However, realty rights being acquired or conveyed by the MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method, unless the property is acquired in its entirety. Property descriptions prepared on behalf of the MHTC must be prepared in a manner that meets the following requirements as outlined in the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) **<u>Section 236.4.6.2</u>** . When acquiring a property in its entirety, the property description shall be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record for the subject property.

Prior to presenting the general warranty deed, quitclaim deed, or other such document to the grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify that the parcel described in the property description corresponds with the right of way plans, and to verify that the right of way plans correspond with the survey information gathered by the professional land surveyor. Needless to say, these descriptions can be long and tedious to write.

The goal of this research project is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to develop a "first draft" of  the legal land description (LLD) using the MHTC parameters. This draft could be reviewed and edited accordingly by MoDOT's Right of Way staff.

item: GC09 Core deliverables include a data management plan, a proof-of-concept demonstration of AI writing legal land descriptions, training and a user manual for ROW staff, and draft and final reports; the final report, summary, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026.
evidence:
client_situation[0] The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) is the issuing body, and the study is performed for MHTC and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing drafts.
client_situation[1] The work is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and the Offeror must fully coordinate its activities with that division.
client_situation[2] MoDOT's Right of Way staff must produce property descriptions that accurately define the land areas or rights acquired, conveyed or leased, reciting specific rights when less than fee simple title.
client_situation[3] Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
client_situation[4] Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2.
client_situation[5] Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify the parcel matches the right of way plans and that those plans match the surveyor's survey information.
client_situation[6] Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the research.
client_situation[7] The business driver is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for producing a "first draft" legal land description (LLD) from MHTC parameters that MoDOT Right of Way staff could review and edit.
goal[0] The client wants a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," that determines whether AI/ML can generate a first draft of a legal land description using MHTC parameters for review and editing by MoDOT Right of Way staff.
goal[1] The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the final invoice due and contract ending February 2, 2026.
goal[2] Task 2 requires a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
goal[3] Task 3b requires the Offeror to name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.
goal[4] Task 3c requires a proof-of-concept demonstration of how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving improvement feedback.
goal[5] Task 4 requires the Offeror to train ROW staff on the finalized system and supply a user manual for staff reference.
goal[6] Task 5 requires a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary plus supporting documentation, and Task 6 requires a final report with all findings, a 1-2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff.
goal[7] Task 1 requires a kick-off meeting, quarterly project status meetings with minutes, and a Data Management Plan submitted within 2 weeks after kick-off.

constraints[6] The Data Management Plan must describe anticipated data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used to ensure maximum future utility of the data.
constraints[7] Award is subject to a post-award negotiated contract that MHTC may cancel if terms cannot be agreed, and the RFP requires 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation targets, an E-Verify affidavit (Exhibit A), lawful-presence affidavits for sole proprietorships and partnerships (Exhibit B), and insurance of $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence for general and automobile liability plus Missouri workers' compensation.
